data.narrative:
Fortera, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Ryan Gilliam, has raised $200M+ to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Helion, Redwood Materials, and three others) and 1 public comparable (LNZA), all within the climate and energy sector at similar or proximate stages.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses total capital raised ($200M) as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement, implying a $340M valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M) yields a median of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in maturity and capital intensity within the climate-tech segment.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $289M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $670M. The 4x spread between low and high reflects material uncertainty around whether Fortera's technology risk profile, commercialization timeline, and capital requirements align closer to earlier-stage or later-stage comp valuations. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to KoBold and Electric Hydrogen, and the sustainability of current fundraising momentum through Series D.
